title: Current RH Proof Direction
limitNote: RH remains open. The independent arithmetic saving needed for the source contradiction has not been proved.
contextScope: The original Riesz carrier preserves squarefree support, Möbius signs, logarithmic phases and complex fibre correlations. Its initial bound now uses the proved critical homogeneous exponent plus any positive epsilon and a negative prime-power allowance. The combined correlation, sampling and normalization cost still needs a source-scale saving. No distance to an RH proof is asserted.
metadataOrigin: Current RH campaign metadata; theorem names and scopes resolve through the compiled project status.

direction.statement: Seek a contradiction at any hypothetical right-half zeta zero by proving an independent estimate incompatible with the original Riesz carrier’s forced source limit. Preserve Möbius signs, logarithmic phases and full frequency correlations through conditioned-energy estimates. Stronger zero-free regions narrow the remaining strip; the arithmetic saving is still open.
direction.changeReason: Establish the dedicated RH campaign view, distinguishing the long-term signed-carrier strategy from its zero-free-region and numerical-certificate work.

latestUpdate.title: A growing prime head now has vanishing correction error in the original band.
latestUpdate.body: Lean now pays the full correction multiplied by every actual head prime up to n+16, at original factorial orders d*n. An explicit bound covers all head families and a positive cofinal stride pays their growth. The literal band, cutoff, phases and negative multiplicity source are preserved. The compensated leading quotient, its mixed correction and signed boundary remain coupled; their joint floor is open.
latestUpdate.next: Next: bound the explicit moving-window residual while retaining correlations between its compensated leading quotient, mixed correction and signed completion boundary.

scopes.boundScope: Furthest checked carrier bound: at a=0,b=1, use the proved critical homogeneous exponent 2k(u+1)-k(k+1)/2+eps for every eps>0, with k>=2,u>=k. The complete initial allowance is at most B*p^beta, -1/2<=beta<0, with every homogeneous and descendant-energy premise discharged. Prime, padded-quotient and p^S<=X conditions are explicit. Constants and thresholds are unevaluated. Full signed correlations, sampling and block normalization remain; their combined saving is unproved. RH remains open.
scopes.sourceScope: Under the displayed hypothetical right-half-zero assumptions, the normalized original carrier has the prescribed negative-multiplicity source limit. This conditional source identity supplies one side of the proposed contradiction; its independent arithmetic counterpart remains open.
scopes.initialConditioningScope: The unweighted critical moment exponent plus every eps>0 holds for k>=2,u>=k at sufficiently large endpoints. For each k>=12 the full eligible degree window gives the actual imaginary-power product sum a saving 1/(128*k^2) throughout M^(2k-2)<=t<=M^(2k), M^4<=z<=4*M^4. Original Dirichlet blocks of length M^4 starting at M^4<=z<=2*M^4 have bound C*M^(4-1/(128*k^2)); every partial block has its explicit endpoint allowance. Both moments, all Gaussian tails, smoothing, Taylor errors and averaging masses are paid. Constants and thresholds are unevaluated for each fixed degree. Uniform degree costs, all-scale zeta growth and the combined Riesz weighted saving remain open. Finite Abel transport also preserves every nonnegative decreasing weight family, including literal zeta coefficients at nonnegative real part. The main term pays actual total weight and the endpoint only its initial weight. All Gaussian constants cost at most two after the actual moment root, uniformly for k>=12; moment constants and thresholds remain unevaluated. Finite descent now proves actual critical+defect moments at every X>=1 with cost A^n*k!, starting from the proved elementary factorial bound. One exponent decrement and one multiplier are chosen before the source exponent and constant. The profile multiplier is at most (2ku)^(7k) independently of iteration count; original C stays linear and outside the prime threshold. The sharper actual deep remainder also retains -defect*u/(u+1)*(b-a+H), upstream of the present half-depth relaxation. The global multiplier, decrement and cutoff depth still need degree bounds; uniform zeta growth and the zero-free union are unchanged.
scopes.exponentAuditScope: Exact normalization audit: after restoring the source scale, lowering the exponent changes only the deep remainder by the coarse-quotient power. Every original intermediate conditioned energy is identical. The complete scaled allowance is no larger when a full coarse window fits. This comparison bounds no intermediate energy and does not prove RH.
scopes.fullRecurrenceScope: The general original-carrier recurrence applies to every displayed finite scale pair a<=b and depth H. Both actual quotient moments use the proved first improved exponent; all intermediate energies remain in the full allowance. The default view uses the critical exponent plus positive epsilon and a proved negative initial profile under its deeper cutoff conditions. No net signed correlation saving or RH contradiction is asserted.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaPrimeCharacterRemain.label: First-order prime core plus exact logarithmic remainder
RiemannGaussian.ZetaPrimeCharacterRemain.summary: A product of small local factors equals the exponential of the first-order core plus the sum of local log errors. The principal logarithm of the whole product is not assumed.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaPrimeCharacterRemain.label: Integrated nonlinear remainder · uniform finite cutoff
RiemannGaussian.ZetaPrimeCharacterRemain.summary: At each fixed Re(s)>1/2 and labels at least 16, the nonlinear log remainder divided by ξ² has a proved cutoff-independent L1 bound. This does not bound the exponential of the first-order core or its factorial filter.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaSquarefreeRieszCompl.label: Sufficient cofinal floor · premise still open
RiemannGaussian.ZetaSquarefreeRieszCompl.summary: A fixed c<1 and Re(B_N)≥−c at arbitrarily large N contradict the original negative multiplicity limit. The independent floor is an unproved premise.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPrimeFourier.ac.label: Original filtered band as a full prime-factor integral
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPrimeFourier.ac.summary: The complete divisor mass and first logarithmic moment of each squarefree nonunit composite are proved zero. Both frequencies, the original band, factorial filter and common physical length remain.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPrimeFourier.te.label: Prime-factor source · conditional on a right-half zero
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPrimeFourier.te.summary: The exact prime-factor integral retains the original negative multiplicity limit under the hypothetical-zero assumption. This source identity supplies no independent lower bound.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPrimeFourier.pr.label: Every prime sine, central phase and prime count retained
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPrimeFourier.pr.summary: The full squarefree prime product equals (2i)^ω times its central logarithmic phase and all real sine factors. This is an exact identity, not a source-scale estimate.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaPrimeNonlinearFactor.label: Integrated multiplicative correction · bounded at fixed real part
RiemannGaussian.ZetaPrimeNonlinearFactor.summary: For labels at least 16 and fixed Re(s)>1/2, exp(E)−1 divided by frequency squared has a finite cutoff-independent integral norm. The factor exp(A) remains outside this bound.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaPrimeNonlinearTail.i.label: Integrated correction paid by a decreasing arithmetic tail
RiemannGaussian.ZetaPrimeNonlinearTail.i.summary: Every finite selection above K costs at most an explicit constant times the remaining summable square-log mass. This bounds the multiplicative correction before multiplication by exp(A) or the factorial filter.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaPrimeNonlinearTail.e.label: Nonlinear prime-tail allowance tends uniformly to zero
RiemannGaussian.ZetaPrimeNonlinearTail.e.summary: For each fixed σ>1/2 and every ε>0, one threshold K≥16 makes the integrated multiplicative correction smaller than ε for every finite Q above K and every s with Re(s)=σ. No uniform limit as σ approaches 1/2 is claimed.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCompositeProduc.label: Composite completion retains exp(A+E)−1−A
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCompositeProduc.summary: The full composite divisor sum is a compensated exponential after proving exact unit and singleton deletion. The local-log identification assumes all participating primes are at least 16.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCompositeProduc.label: The actual finite band retains its entire completion boundary
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCompositeProduc.summary: The canonical primorial contains every original squarefree band label. Its complete composite response minus the explicit omitted signed sum recovers that band exactly; no smallness of the boundary is asserted.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFixedCofactor.t.label: Fixed composite cofactor · full original-band decay

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFixedCofactor.t.label: Clipped prime insertion · actual filtered decay

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFixedCofactor.n.label: Explicit inverse-order and geometric arithmetic allowance

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPrimeClasses.on.label: One large prime · a nonunit divisor of 30030
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPrimeClasses.on.summary: Every actual squarefree composite with one large prime is p*a, where p>=16 is prime, a>1 divides 30030 and p does not divide a.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPrimeClasses.pr.label: The six possible prime cofactors

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFixedCofactor.c.label: Surviving semiprime coefficient · exact formula
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFixedCofactor.c.summary: For a prime cofactor a and log(a)<=L<=log(p), the actual coefficient is -log(p*a)*log(a)/L. Its signed filtered tail is not bounded by the composite-cofactor theorem.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaPrimeNonlinearHalfpl.label: Nonlinear correction · uniform closed-half-plane decay
RiemannGaussian.ZetaPrimeNonlinearHalfpl.summary: For every fixed sigma>1/2 the integrated nonlinear multiplier allowance tends to zero uniformly on Re(s)>=sigma and all finite larger-label selections. The exp(A) coupling remains unpaid.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFilteredComplet.label: Completed response and boundary · full factorial filter
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFilteredComplet.summary: Every original factorial moment passes through the exact completed-minus-boundary response inside the paired Fourier integral. The whole quotient is integrable; no separate channel bound is asserted.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszReducedCofactor.label: Finite composite head · whole union decays
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszReducedCofactor.summary: The full finite union of composite cofactors dividing 30030 is paid inside one original-band sum, without counting overlaps twice.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszReducedCofactor.label: Finite deletion · original source retained

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszReducedCofactor.label: Conditional closure to RH · arithmetic floor remains a premise
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszReducedCofactor.summary: For each hypothetical right-half zero, the displayed strict cofinal lower floor would contradict its source. Reflection then gives Mathlib RH. This theorem does not prove the floor.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszGrowingCofactor.label: Eighth-power budget · source-scale decay
